text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; I need to determine if this is due to a surgical emergency. Is the vomiting truly bilious, or is it green? When did these symptoms start, and are you passing any stools?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus.

The presence of bilious vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise; your brother's history of pyloric stenosis is a red herring, as pyloric stenosis does not cause bilious vomiting. I need to confirm if the baby is passing meconium or any stool at all, and I will immediately request an Upper GI series to check for intestinal malrotation. REQUEST TEST: Upper GI Series.
